SEC-01 // Core Stats

Attributes & Modifiers

Seven characteristics encompass the potential of your character. Each (except Luck) starts at 40, average by human standards. The tens value of a characteristic is your Attribute Bonus, which drives much of play: a Toughness score of 43 gives a Toughness Bonus of 4. Pushing a stat over the next bonus threshold (say 48 → 53) can pay off in many ways, and may be worth the XP.

STR

Strength

Ability to lift, carry, push and pull. Fuels the heaviest armor and weapons, improves all melee damage, and has the largest impact on carry weight.

AGI

Agility

Dexterity and finesse. Governs quick movement, initiative, and taking enemies by surprise. Precise melee weapons require and reward high Agility.

TGH

Toughness

Resilience to physical and mental trauma. Survive lethal injuries, shrug off status effects, and resist being worn down by GENESIS terror tactics. Aids carry capacity.

CHA

Charisma

Strength of personality. Builds ties with the resistance and defectors, powers bluffs and disguises, and drives Paraphysics.

LCK

Luck

An intangible edge set by fate, it cannot be raised by normal means. Feeds initiative and grants luck points that can bend the outcome of a roll.

INT

Intelligence

Reasoning and applied knowledge. Understand xenotech, hack security, treat wounds without supplies, power paraphysics, and resist mental intrusion.

PER

Perception

Strength of the senses; the backbone of ranged accuracy. Detect ambushes and poison, and land critical hits with any weapon.

Species

Each species carries its own strengths, weaknesses, and considerations, don't take the choice lightly. Species perks are granted automatically at enlistment and appear on your sheet.

Humans Sol System · Earth

Humanity's adaptability is second to none. Individual galactic species may hold an edge in a few attributes, but that usually comes at the cost of others. Humans are consistent across the board, making them some of the most well-rounded fighters and operatives around.

Mutant (Baron) Sol System · Earth

A Baron is the rare mutant who came through transformation with their human silhouette and most of their old mind intact. Where a Vassal cannot set foot in a settlement without drawing weapons, a Baron can walk through a market, sit across a negotiating table, or take a contract, their nature passing unnoticed by all but the most careful eye. This makes them their tribe's emissaries to the human world, and it is exactly what makes them suited to a resistance cell.

What brings a Baron to the fight varies. Some are emissaries whose trade routes turned into alliances. Some are mercenaries who took a job and stayed. Some are climbing toward Monarchhood and see GENESIS as the surest proving ground. Barons are the only playable mutant caste.

Species Perks

Controlled Mutations: Roll twice on the Positive Mutation Table and once on the Negative Mutation Table at character creation. Because a Baron's mutations are bestowed under a Monarch's careful guidance, you may reroll the Negative result once and take the second outcome. All results are permanent. If a mutation grants a skill you already have, increase that skill by one rank instead. (See the Mutation Tables page.)

Human Passing: A Baron reads as an ordinary (if slightly off-putting) human under normal observation. Gain an Assistance die on Deception and disguise checks to maintain a human cover, and move through human settlements and most GENESIS checkpoints without automatic suspicion. Openly using overt mutations (wings, bared natural weapons, acid spit, and the like) immediately blows this cover to any human witnesses.

Humanoid Frame: Unlike Vassals, a Baron's build lets them wear manufactured armor and use standard gear normally, with no special modification or cost penalty.

Murk-Eye: A mutant's eyes have a special adaptation to poor light. They suffer no D.M. penalty or skill check penalty due to low light conditions, and can see up to 14 tiles of darkness as if it is standard Night Vision. Complete darkness can still apply penalties to checks.

Latent Claws: A Baron can call forth natural weapons at will: 1d6 + AGI or STR modifier damage, Light quality, undisarmable. Doing so in the open marks them as a mutant (see Human Passing).

Telestoi Eridani System · Elysthae

A proud and magnetic people, who won the Ascension Wars on their home world 5000 years ago. Victory made them complacent and softened their edges. Now, having lost that home to the Overlords, they have traveled through the Stellar Doors. One such door led to Earth, a place where they will learn to fight once more.

The nearest kin to humans of any species, they stand from 5'2" to 6'6". Their skin runs a stone gradient from marble white through gray to onyx, their eyes gold, blue, purple, red or green, and their pointed ears move with their mood.

Species Perks

Telestoian Glamor: You impose a chosen self-image on the minds around you: a disguise as a humanoid near your own build. It cannot make you invisible, or show something far from your true shape. It holds as long as you are conscious and keep 3 Energy committed to it: while it holds, those 3 cannot be spent, and it falls if you have fewer than 3 left. Disorientated does not break it. It is a paraphysical effect on minds, so it does nothing to mind-immune creatures, and cameras and recordings show your true face. Other means can see through it, as the GM rules: a Paraphysics check to notice an anomaly, or another's paraphysical senses. Use this ability to raise the Glamor, and again to let it fall.

Memory Sharing: Out of combat, with a willing creature you touch, you give or receive one memory, lived as if it were their own: a face, a route walked, a conversation, what happened in a room.

Empath: You feel the emotions around you, and can lean on them. Once per session, choose one: add Assistance dice equal to your Paraphysics skill rank to a Persuasion or Insight check, or grant an ally -20 D.M. on their check to break out of the Panicked state.

Gifted Mind: Your people's gift runs deeper than most. You start with rank 1 in Optics and in Telepathy, and in those two disciplines your rank can reach 6 where others stop at 5. Both count toward the three disciplines a Telestoi can hold, so your third is yours to choose.

Telesma: The bioluminescent organ that wraps your head shows what you are: bright in youth and dim with age, cool colors when you are well and hot ones when you are hurt or sick. It pulses when you use paraphysics: casting a power ends any Concealment you have. Your Glamor holds through it.

House Scion

Born to the noble family of a Telestoi city-state. You were raised on debate, sport and art, the arenas where your people settled every quarrel for five thousand years instead of going to war. You know how to win without a weapon.

Settled by Contest: Once per session, you can challenge a willing rival who is not GENESIS to settle a dispute by contest instead of violence: debate, sport or art, at the GM's check. Win, and they honor the terms.

Door Warden

Raised on the temporary homeworld after the Exodus, in the service that keeps the Stellar Doors and the drones that watched Earth for a quarter century. You came through the Earth Door knowing this planet's last twenty five years better than most of the people living on it.

Reticulons Reti System · Reti VI

Brilliant, frail and paraphysically strong. Survivors of when the Overlords stole their shorelines, they spent sixty years adrift in the Ithelû flotilla. They now come to Earth looking for allies, and perhaps a new home.

Reti VI pulls only 0.7 Earth gravity, so their muscles are weaker than a human's and their bones are hollow, like a bird's: a help in the water, a frailty on land. They are lithe and wiry, with sleek, faintly wet skin in greens, teals, blues and tans, an elongated head with fin-like frills, and a large pair of eyes with a smaller second pair above them.

The Enduring Calm

An initiate of the Ishelûvae, the order the old Vaeshelûn monks became in the flight. You were trained the way your people learned they must be: martial discipline first, because paraphysics used wrongly is devastating. You will fight, but you will not ruin a living place for nothing.

Still Water: The order teaches the gift's dangers before its uses. Once per mission, reroll a failed Paraphysics improvisation check, and a Defeat on it counts as a plain failure.

Tidecraft: Out of combat, once per mission, you shape a body of water you can see, up to the size of a room: part it, still it, or draw it into a wall or a bridge for a few minutes.

Flotilla Born

Sixty years between the stars, running from system to system ahead of the Xargryr. You grew up aboard the Ithelû flotilla: patching ships that should have died, staying silent, and listening to enemy traffic. That is how your people found Earth.

Skills: Technology, Mechanics, Xenotechnology, Hacking, Stealth, Survivalism

Patch It Till It Flies: Once per mission, outside combat, you get one broken machine working again for the rest of the scene: a vehicle, a door mechanism, a generator, a radio. It fails for good afterward.

Signal Intercept: Once per mission, you listen in on Xargryr or GENESIS traffic nearby, and the GM tells you one thing it says: a patrol route, a reinforcement time, or an order.

Shipwright: When you are assigned to an Engineering project, you count Mechanics and Xenotechnology at +10 per skill rank instead of +5.

Khaldar Tau Ceti System · Töörzam

A stout and incredibly hardy race, perhaps one of the toughest within the local cluster, and brilliant material scientists. They stand 3'5" to 4'10", dense under thick overlapping plates of keratin, and sense heat through the stone around them.

You can also repair armor mid battle: once per scene, spend an action to restore 1 point of shredded DR on yourself or an adjacent ally.

Stone Gut: You can draw sustenance from minerals and never need rations where stone is available. You gain -10 D.M. on tests to resist ingested poisons and disease.

SEC-03.A // Role Dossier

Legionary

Frontline · Holds the line

The Legionary doctrine is the backbone of the ODR's combat effectiveness, and it was built to be exactly that. Drawn from a long tradition of standard infantry practice across Earth's military institutions, the doctrine was refined and elevated by Colonel Emmrich von Strauss into something considerably more capable than its origins might suggest.

The Legionary does not specialize in the way other ODR doctrines do. That is not a weakness. It is the point. Where other roles demand rare aptitude or years of narrowly focused development, the Legionary doctrine is engineered for accessibility and adaptability. It can be taught broadly, trained efficiently, and deployed across virtually any operational context without degradation in effectiveness. No other doctrine in the ODR's order of battle scales as readily or as reliably.

Within that framework, however, the ceiling is considerable. A seasoned Legionary is equally capable of assuming tactical command of a squad engagement, operating as a unit's pointman in high-risk forward positions, or serving as the hard answer to any threat foolish enough to target their squadmates. The role adapts to the operator, and the operator adapts to the mission.

It may lack the prestige of more specialized doctrines. Senior leadership does not concern itself with that distinction. The Legionary is the most consistently deployable asset in the ODR's inventory, and at full development, it is among the most dangerous. An army built on a foundation this reliable does not require glamour. It requires results.

SEC-03.B // Role Dossier

Marauder

Aggression · Close pressure

The Marauder doctrine did not emerge from a planning room or a strategic review board. It emerged from a wheat field outside Coffeyville, Kansas, on a fog-covered November morning, when Senior Operator Deke Ragnarson made a decision that would permanently alter the ODR's approach to close-quarters combat.

By the latter years of the invasion, the psychological cost of sustained combat operations had become a measurable factor in unit effectiveness. The enemy understood this. Their methods of engagement were deliberately calibrated to exploit fear, and against conventional doctrine, that exploitation was working. Ragnarson identified the problem and arrived at a characteristically direct solution: remove fear from the equation entirely.

What followed was the formation of the Marauder doctrine, built around operators who either lack a conventional fear response or have subordinated it entirely to combat drive. Where other doctrines maintain distance and exploit range, Marauders close it. Armed with hard-hitting short-range weapons and chemical throwers, they bring the fight to a proximity that most opponents are not prepared for. A subset of Marauder operators push this further still, operating in a state of sustained combat aggression that draws more than a passing comparison to historical accounts of battlefield berserkers.

The psychological effect on enemy combatants has been documented and is not insignificant. An enemy that weaponizes fear does not easily adapt to opponents who demonstrate none. Marauders have been observed producing hesitation and disorganization in forces that held cohesion against every other ODR element brought against them.

The tactical application is straightforward. Identify the problem. Send a Marauder. The problem resolves itself.

SEC-03.C // Role Dossier

Specialist

Tech · Utility & support

Every combat doctrine in the ODR's order of battle is built around the capacity to engage and destroy the enemy. The Specialist doctrine is built around keeping everyone else alive long enough to do it.

Specialists are the force multipliers that operate beneath the surface of every successful engagement. They do not often make the after action headlines. What they do is ensure there is an after action report to write. Functioning as the operational core of any ODR fire team, a Specialist's contributions span three critical roles that no competent commander treats as optional.

In the medical capacity, Specialists provide frontline trauma care that directly determines casualty outcomes in the field. Personnel that would otherwise be lost are stabilized, recovered, and returned to the fight. In the engineering capacity, Specialists maintain equipment under combat conditions and construct field fortifications that extend a unit's ability to hold contested terrain. And for those oriented toward offensive application, Specialist sappers demonstrate a proficiency with explosive ordnance that is unmatched across any other ODR doctrine. In their hands, a grenade is far from a risky last resort.

Experienced ODR operators do not debate the value of the Specialist. They have seen what a squad looks like without one. Attrition climbs, positions become untenable and momentum stalls. The Specialist is not a support role in the secondary sense of the word. They are the reason a fire team remains a fire team when the situation deteriorates. No doctrine in the ODR's inventory is more quietly essential.

SEC-03.D // Role Dossier

Outrider

Mobility · Flank & scout

Where other ODR doctrines are employed as a hammer, the Outriders are the scalpel. Representing the highest standard of precision operators within the ODR's order of battle, Outrider doctrine is built around a singular principle: the right target, eliminated at the right moment, with minimal margin for error.

Outriders demonstrate exceptional proficiency across a demanding range of disciplines, including long-range marksmanship, advanced reconnaissance, covert infiltration, and close-quarters gunfighting techniques drawn from a lineage of old-school combat traditions that have proven as effective today as ever. Few doctrines demand the same breadth of individual skill from a single operator.

Tactically, Outriders perform at peak effectiveness when operating in concert with other ODR elements. While allied forces absorb enemy attention and pressure, Outrider operators are free to acquire and engage high-priority targets with a level of precision and composure that disrupts enemy command, coordination, and morale at the source. They do not win battles by brute force. They win them by removing the pieces that hold the enemy together.

A subset of Outrider operators redirect that precision inward, dedicating their skills to the protection of allied personnel on the battlefield. These individuals have developed a reputation among ODR units that borders on reverence. In the chaos of a contested engagement, the sudden crack of a suppressed round dropping a threat before it is even identified is a reminder that somewhere out there, an Outrider is watching. For the soldiers fortunate enough to operate alongside them, that knowledge alone is worth something.

SEC-03.E // Role Dossier

Warmachine

Heavy · Firepower

The Warmachines earned their designation. No other element in the ODR's order of battle carries the same capacity for sustained destruction and battlefield endurance, and no other role demands as much from the operators who fill it. The doctrine traces back to Beau Sterling, an American ODR Officer with an obsessive dedication to firepower and the will to absorb punishment that most soldiers simply don't possess.

Early in the invasion, command kept Warmachine assets in limited rotation, a decision that would be revisited. By mid-campaign, it became clear that certain engagements required something the standard line couldn't provide: the ability to drive overwhelming, unrelenting fire into an enemy position and keep it there until the threat was broken. Warmachines stepped into that gap and didn't step back.

What command didn't fully anticipate was the range of that contribution. Once the shooting stopped and a zone was secured, Warmachines didn't stand down. They dug in and their turret systems turned freshly taken ground into fortified positions, giving the rest of the unit something solid to hold behind. Taking a battle zone is one thing. Keeping it is another. As many learned in World War 1. Warmachines can effectively do both.

Their presence on the line also has a noted measurable impact on the soldiers fighting beside them. Morale holds longer, units will push harder. The effect is difficult to quantify but impossible to ignore after you've seen it in the field.

A single effective Warmachine can alter the outcome of a firefight. Integrate one into a coordinated ODR combined arms push, and the results become something the enemy has a difficult time finding a reliable answer for.

SEC-03.F // Role Dossier

Vanguard

Assault · Breach & lead

Of all the doctrines fielded by the ODR, the Vanguard is the one that required the most convincing. A return to melee-oriented combat in the context of a modern invasion was not a proposal that moved easily through the chain of command. The early objections were reasonable. The results were not what the objectors anticipated.

The Vanguard doctrine is built on a deliberate rejection of ranged engagement as a primary method of contact. Where other ODR elements establish distance and apply firepower, the Vanguard closes it, bringing edged weapons and impact tools directly into the enemy's position. In practice, this approach bifurcates along two equally effective lines. Offensive Vanguards drive into enemy formations to disrupt, dismantle, and eliminate at close quarters, operating with a level of aggression that consistently destabilizes prepared positions. Defensive Vanguards anchor themselves alongside allied personnel and function as a hardened barrier that enemy forces have repeatedly failed to breach.

A third application has been documented with enough frequency to warrant formal acknowledgment. Certain Vanguard operators have issued direct challenges to enemy commanders in the field, engaging in single combat. The tactical implications of these engagements, regardless of outcome, have demonstrated a measurable effect on enemy unit cohesion and morale that conventional engagement methods do not replicate.

Beyond disruption and defense, the Vanguard doctrine revealed an intelligence dividend that was not anticipated in early assessments. Operating at contact range exposed gaps in enemy defensive architecture that ranged engagement had never uncovered. Vanguards also proved to be an effective counter to the enemy's own melee-capable combatants, a threat category that other ODR doctrines were not always configured to address efficiently.

The doctrine was called a terrible idea by those who had not seen it employed. That assessment did not survive contact with the evidence.

SEC-07 // Resolution

Combat Rolls

Attack rolls and resistance checks use a percentile d100 system. Skill checks use the DYNOSRS dice pool instead, see the Skills section.

d100: Attacks & Resistance

Attack rolls and resistance checks use a 1d100 system. For a ranged attack you roll a d100 and must meet or roll under your Perception attribute. Raising an attribute directly raises your chance to succeed. The rule is constant; only the opposed attribute changes with context.

  • Melee attacks normally check against Strength.
  • Resisting a flashbang checks against Toughness.
  • Paraphysics generally checks against Charisma.

Difficulty Modifiers (D.M.)

How D.M. Affects a d100 Check
Negative (−) D.M.Positive (+) D.M.
EffectMakes the check easier to pass.Makes the check harder to pass.
Example // d100 Attack

Alan shoots a GENESIS trooper behind half cover with an Assault Rifle. His Perception is 45. Half cover grants +30; the weapon's accuracy grants −15.

1d100 + 30 (Cover) − 15 (Accuracy)
45 + 30 − 15 = 60

Checked against his Perception of 45, this is a miss.

SEC-08 // Skill System

Skills: DYNOSRS

The Dynamic Overall Skill Roll System (DYNOSRS) is a dice pool system used to generate non-binary outcomes for skill-based challenges. A binary system leaves only a pass or fail state, often with little chance to mechanically support successful results that carry downsides, or a failed check that still comes out with some advantage.

Dice Types

There are six dice types across three sizes. Each pairs a positive die (your pool) with an opposing die of the same size.

Faces: 2 blanks · 3 successes · 6 edges
Hindrance
d8Opposing

Represents some small hindrance a character must overcome, a glitch in a computer terminal, an unexpected crunch on time, or the stress a character feels in the moment.

Faces: 2 blanks · 3 failures · 5 dangers
Aptitude
d10Positive

A character's innate, attribute-based talent toward a skill. Take the attribute the skill uses (History uses Intelligence), divide its modifier by 2, and round down. Most humans start with a modifier of 4, giving 2 skill dice on a check.

Faces: 1 blank · 7 successes · 9 edges
Difficulty
d10Opposing

The base challenge a check rolls against, largely set by the environment. Climbing a wall in a quiet alley is a much easier check than defusing a GENESIS explosive in the middle of heavy gunfire.

Faces: 1 blank · 6 failures · 9 dangers
Skill
d12Positive

A character's trained ability in a skill. It can also represent emergent circumstances, an "Ah Ha!" moment, an expert in the field helping you, a really well-built tool, or Lady Luck smiling on you during a check.

Faces: 1 blank · 12 successes · 9 edges · 1 victory
Obstacle
d12Opposing

Significant resistance against a successful check, an alien UFO bearing down on a strafing run, an incredibly sensitive alarm system, or overwhelming stress mounting to get something done quickly.

Faces: 1 blank · 10 failures · 11 dangers · 1 defeat

Dice Symbols

Six symbols each represent a possible outcome. To read a roll, find the symbols that cancel one another out, remove them from the pool, and the remainder is the actual result of the check.

✓
Success

A check mark counts toward a successful roll. You only need a single success left after cancellation for the check to pass.

▲
Edge

A build-up in momentum or morale. Not always counted toward pass/fail, but can be spent to make the immediate outcome more favorable. Bank up to three Edges for other options during the mission; all banked Edge resets to 0 at session's end.

★
Victory

The most powerful player symbol, found on a single face of the Skill die. On an otherwise failed roll it converts a failure into a success. On a passed check it can instead be banked (one at a time) for more powerful options. Resets to 0 at session's end.

✗
Failure

Rolled on an opposing die, it counts toward an unsuccessful roll. A check is failed if at least one failure symbol remains after everything is calculated.

▼
Danger

A build-up in the tense, uncertain nature of the world. Usually not counted toward pass/fail, but the GM can spend it to make an outcome less favorable, or bank up to six Dangers for use during the mission. Resets to 0 at session's end.

☠
Defeat

The most powerful symbol against a player, found on a single face of the Obstacle die. The GM can turn a passed check into a failure, or bank it (one at a time). The banked Defeat is lost when the mission or session ends.

Opposing Symbols

Paired symbols cancel one another out. Remove matched pairs, then read what's left.

Cancellation Pairs
PositiveCancelsNegative
✓ Success⇄✗ Failure
▲ Edge⇄▼ Danger
★ Victory⇄☠ Defeat

Resolving a Check

Example // Paraphysics Check

Ragnar makes a Paraphysics check with 2 Skill and 1 Aptitude dice versus 2 Difficulty. He rolls:

Skill Dice 1: ✓ ✓ ✓
Skill Dice 2: ✓ ▲
Aptitude Dice 1: ✓ ▲ ▲
Difficulty Dice 1: ✗ ✗ ▼
Difficulty Dice 2: ✗ ▼
Final Result: ✓ ✓ ▲

After cancellation, the result is 2 successes and 1 edge, a pass with a little momentum banked.

NOTE // Foundry VTT automatically parses out the final result, so there's no manual calculating for players or GMs.

When the final result shows no success or failure, the check simply requires a little more time in most cases. If the situation is time-sensitive and only a single check is allowed, the roll's total remaining positive symbols versus negative symbols instead convert to successes and failures. In the rare event the roll is left a total wash, the skill challenge is rerolled as if for the first time.

Upgrading Aptitude Dice

All skills are trainable up to four times total. Each point trained increases the skill at a 1-to-1 scale up to your modifier total. Train a skill past your modifier and you add an additional aptitude die. Once you raise the governing attribute to match your skill level, that aptitude die automatically upgrades to a skill die.

Example // Upgrading

Ragnar has a Charisma modifier of 5, so his base skill total for Persuasion is 2. Having trained the skill 3 times, he rolls 2 Skill (d12) and 1 Aptitude (d10). As soon as he raises his Charisma modifier to 6, he simply rolls 3 Skill (d12).

Skill Rank Increase Costs

Skill Rank Cost
Rank 1Rank 2Rank 3Rank 4
20 XP40 XP60 XP80 XP

You pay the XP required by the rank you're upgrading to, for example, going from Rank 2 to Rank 3 costs 60 XP.

Creation //

The maximum skill rank at character creation is Rank 2. Any further ranks must be purchased after creation is complete (this includes starting XP granted), unless the GM states players may raise ranks beyond 2 at creation.

Skill Check Difficulty

A challenge's difficulty varies with circumstance and environment, and the GM sets it based mainly on what the character is attempting. Picking a simple lock might always be a standard check, while external factors add Hindrances and Obstacles rather than simply raising the base difficulty.

Difficulty: Dice Used
DifficultyDice Used
Easy1 Difficulty Dice
Normal2 Difficulty Dice
Hard3 Difficulty Dice
Challenging4 Difficulty Dice
Formidable5 Difficulty Dice
Nigh Impossible6 Difficulty Dice
Gate //

A Nigh Impossible check can only be attempted when a character in the active squad holds a Victory Point to allow it.

The GM can also raise difficulty outside the standard scale, typically by adding Hindrance dice for small environmental challenges (some perks negate these), or by spending banked Dangers and Defeats to upgrade a check's Difficulty dice into Obstacle dice.

Opposed Checks & Contests

Opposed Checks

When directly opposed by an NPC, instead of an arbitrary GM-defined difficulty, the NPC's Aptitude and Skill dice become the PC's Difficulty and Obstacle dice.

Competitive Checks

When two characters (PC or NPC) compete, each rolls as normal. Success is no longer binary, count the number of Successes, and whoever was "most" successful wins. Ties are broken by Victory's, then Edge.

Banked Edge, Danger, Victory & Defeat

A player character can bank up to 3 Edges and 1 Victory; a GM can bank up to 6 Dangers and 1 Defeat. These resources exist mainly for cinematic flare, to help or hinder skill-challenge scenes and, on occasion, tactical battles. Edges aren't as strong as Victory or Luck points, but regenerate more reliably and are used in smaller ways; the same goes for Danger versus Defeat.

Banked Resource Uses

Depending on how many Edge points a character has banked, they can spend a variable amount to garner different options both in and outside of combat.

Player Resources

▲ One Edge
  1. Add an additional assistance dice to a skill check that you are actively making. This can be applied once per skill check. Other assistance dice can be added to the same check if they originate from other sources such as items or perks.
  2. Reduce the modifier on a D100 check by 5. Only usable once per check.
  3. Restore 2 energy. This can be used multiple times in a single round.
  4. Perform an additional quick action in the same round that is not a skill check.
▲ Two Edges
  1. Perform an additional skill check in a single round.
  2. Add an additional assistance dice to someone else's skill check. This can only be applied once per skill check, and can stack with other sources such as perks and items but not with someone using their own Edge to add an assistance dice.
  3. Increase the modifier on any D100 check by 5. Only usable once per check.
▲ Three Edges
  1. Upgrade one Aptitude dice to a Skill dice on a check you make.
  2. Reduce the modifier on a D100 check by 10. Only usable once per check, not stackable with the 5 point option.
  3. Grant yourself a free reload action.
  4. Downgrade a difficulty dice to a hindrance dice for another creature's check.
★ Victory
  1. Replicate any of the Edge actions.
  2. Move your standard speed outside of your turn.
  3. Reduce the total difficulty check of a skill challenge you roll by 1.
  4. Guarantee a critical hit.
  5. Adjust the modifier of any D100 check by 15. This can be stacked with Edge uses as long as the Edge is spent by another character.
  6. Cancel out the use of a Defeat point used by a GM. Note the GM is unable to cancel the use of Victory dice.

GM Resources

▼ One Danger
  1. Replicate anything a player can do with One Edge. (Assistance turns to Hindrance).
▼ Two Danger
  1. Increase the modifier on any D100 check by 5. Only usable once per check.
  2. Allow a free half movement to a creature outside of their turn.
  3. Reduce the effectiveness of cover by one degree (Full > Half, Half > None) for a single attack.
▼ Three Danger
  1. Upgrade one difficulty dice to an Obstacle Dice on a creature's skill check.
  2. Grant any NPC creature a free reload.
  3. Adjust the modifier of any D100 check by 10.
  4. Allow an enemy to Hunker Down outside of their turn.
  5. Re-roll damage done by an attack.
☠ Defeat
  1. Replicate any of the Danger actions.
  2. Destroy 1 tile of cover.
  3. Allow a full movement for any creature outside of their turn.
  4. Allow a creature to take a non-attack action outside of their turn.
  5. Grant the GM a re-roll on any dice check.
  6. Halve the damage done to a creature.
  7. Purge any and all negative effects on a creature at the start of their turn before any effects or damage is calculated.

Starting Danger & Edge

Given the state of the world and the missions Eclipse finds itself in, there's always some level of danger. At the start of any mission the GM rolls a 1d6 to set how much Danger they've banked going in, to spend as they see fit.

Starting Edge is determined by a coin flip or a 1d2: on a 1, all characters begin with one banked Edge; on a 2, none. The squad may make a single check for everyone or roll individually, but they must state which before any starting Edge is determined.

pages.name: Action Types
pages.html:
SEC-09 // Economy

Action Types

Each turn a character has two action points and one reaction before any circumstantial modifiers. Some actions end your turn regardless of points remaining; others cost one and don't; others require both. Reactions can trigger at any time, only in response to specific events.

Dual Actions

Require greater focus and dedication. Typically high-impact or non-standard, firing a sniper rifle or abilities like "Pour it On." Shift movements do not prevent dual actions.

Turn-Ending

Always end your turn, even with points or quick actions to spare. Firing a weapon, some special abilities, and grenades, unless a perk like "Light 'Em Up" says otherwise.

Single Actions

Done quickly and easily. Use one of your two action points and do not end your turn. Moving your speed and abilities like "Aid Protocol" are single actions.

Quick Actions

Require no particular effort and can often be done off-turn, removing a hat, dropping an item, replying to a taunt. Those needing your turn carry the Active Character subtype (e.g. "Lightning Hands").

Reactions

Only in response to an event, such as an overwatch shot. Each character has one reaction per round unless a perk or item says otherwise. Always available, even to the active character. Dodging does not count as a reaction.

pages.name: Combat Actions
pages.html:
SEC-10 // On Your Turn

Combat Actions

Every action carries one or more subtypes that inform when it can be used. Concentration actions can't be used while disorientated; Movement actions are unusable while immobilized.

Attack
Varies · Turn-EndingMelee / Ranged

Make a melee or ranged attack roll. A success grants a single hit on the enemy.

Sprint
Two Actions · Turn-EndingMovement

Move up to your Sprint speed in one move. While running, any reaction fire you trigger takes +15 to its attack roll.

Disengage
One ActionMovement

Safely break from melee. Move up to your Run speed without provoking opportunity attacks. A ranged attack after disengaging takes +20. Some perks and enemies bypass this immunity.

Dive for Cover
ReactionMovement

When attacked by a ranged weapon while fully out of cover and not flanked, dive behind nearby cover. The attack resolves as normal; afterward, hit or miss, move tiles equal to your Shift speed.

Fire Rocket
1-2 Actions · Turn-EndingAttack

Use a rocket launcher on a target. Both action points grant −20 accuracy; one action takes +20. On a hit the rocket lands exactly where aimed; a miss scatters per the launched rules.

Hunker Down
1 Action · Turn-EndingDefensive

In cover, boost all cover benefits until your next turn. No help against flankers. Ranged attacks on you suffer +30, and you get −30 to dodge.

Item Usage
1 ActionVaries

Use a medkit, throw a grenade, etc., generally 1 action. Any damaging item is turn-ending by default; any health-restoring item is not.

Improvise
VariesVaries

For anything the rules don't cover, negotiate with the DM on whether it's possible and its consequences. The DM's verdict is final, but unhealthy precedents can be overturned.

Move
1 ActionMovement

Move up to your Run range (4 + AGI Mod). Moving while engaged in melee provokes an opportunity attack from the engaging enemy.

Overwatch
1 Action · Turn-Ending · ReactionAttack · Concentration · Ranged

Watch for the moment to strike. React-fire on the first enemy moving more than one tile, at +15. Can trigger on revealed enemies. Usually can't crit, some perks change this.

Reload
VariesMiscellaneous

Reload a ranged weapon; some take one action, others two. You may only reload weapons you're using or emplacements, never a weapon held by another character.

Shift
Quick ActionMovement · Active Character

Move two tiles (plus armor bonuses). Doesn't block two-action abilities, but can trigger reaction fire. Using Shift forfeits Run and Sprint. Peeking one tile isn't a shift if you return before acting.

Suppressing Fire
1 Action · Turn-EndingAttack · Concentration · Ranged

With an LMG, AR, or SMG (needs ≥2 ammo allotments), pin a target. Their tests take +30 and their attack range drops to two tiles, paraphysics unaffected. Moving >1 tile in sight triggers a free attack (no ammo, not reaction fire).

Shield Wall
1 ActionDefensive

Grant yourself and any creature within 1 tile behind you Half Cover in one declared facing. Perks can change its overall effectiveness.

Dodge
Quick ActionDefensive

A non-reaction Agility test to halve a hit's damage (rounded down). Out of cover, dodge rolls take +30. On a crit, halve rolled damage then add crit bonus. Starting Dodge Pool 1 per turn, refreshed at turn's end.

Help
1 ActionSupport

Adjacent to an ally, let them reroll a check against a negative condition they carry, panicked, ignited, and the like.

pages.name: Battlefield Modifiers
pages.html:
SEC-11 // Terrain & Positioning

Battlefield Modifiers

Factors to weigh before taking a shot or breaking into the open.

Cover

Cover is a lifeline, half or full, sticking to it saves lives. Each style confers a defense bonus against incoming fire and eases dodging a hit.

Cover Modifiers
No CoverHalf CoverFull Cover
Accuracy D.M.0+30+45
Critical Chance D.M.0+30+45
Dodge D.M.+30−15−30

Cover Types & Destruction

A missed shot has a 50% chance to damage cover, flip a 1d2, and on a 2 it's damaged. Durability is measured in failure points (FP). Refer to a weapon's Ballistics section for how much damage it deals to cover.

Cover Durability
FlimsyStandardDurable
ExamplesFences, trash cansConcrete barriers, walls, trees, carsGENESIS fortifications, heavy vehicles
Half Cover FP135
Full Cover FP246
Exposed

Taking fire from a direction you have no cover against, ambushed or flanked. Attacks gain −15 crit chance, and some perks don't apply while exposed.

Engaged in Melee

Both fighters are engaged once a melee attack is made. Leaving without Disengage provokes an opportunity attack. Ranged attacks while engaged take +20 (unless Light), or +40 for Cumbersome weapons.

High Ground

Attacking a lower target grants −10; attacking a higher target suffers +10.

Disorientated

+20 to offensive actions and dodges, speed halved (rounded down), no Concentration actions, and any maintained concentration breaks.

Smoke, Fog, etc.

+20 accuracy to hit a target within it. Characters inside gain +3 to stealth checks that end in the smoke or fog.

Suppressed

+20 to accuracy tests; item and ability range capped at two tiles. Paraphysical abilities are unaffected by suppression.

Unaware

Attacks gain −20 accuracy and reaction fire takes no penalty. An unaware character can still react and dodge, but dodge rolls are treated as out of cover.

pages.name: Soldier's Luck
pages.html:
SEC-12 // Fate

Soldier's Luck

Luck points are your character's drive to retake the world, an intangible edge to bend the odds or steer a disaster. You have luck points equal to your Luck modifier, spent as a quick action.

  • Reroll a check or attack roll.
  • Add your Luck Modifier to a skill check, may be done after a failure is determined.
  • Set your initiative to 10 + AGI Bonus at the start of combat.
  • Instantly heal Health equal to your Toughness mod. Once per mission.
  • Instantly regain Energy equal to your Charisma + Intelligence mods. Once per mission.
  • Purge all negative conditions on your turn, done at turn start, before any negative effects trigger.
  • Make a critical hit check with −50 to the check.
  • Re-roll a scatter test.
  • When instantly killed, instead set HP to 0 and begin bleeding out. Once per mission.

pages.name: Soldier Energy
pages.html:
SEC-13 // Resource

Soldier Energy

Energy counterbalances the power of Active Abilities. Total capacity equals 10 + CHA Bonus + INT Bonus, full at the start of a mission.

Manage //

Energy is difficult to replenish. Active Abilities supplement tactical combat, they don't replace careful thinking. A soldier who squanders energy at the first opportunity may find themselves without the means to save their own life when it matters most.

SEC-15 // Armor

Defenses

The sword always seeks a way through armor, but armor does much to keep you alive. Every basic armor offers defensive boons worth understanding.

Heavy Kevlar Armor Cost: 80 Credits

The highest defensive bonuses of the basic armors, at the price of weight and being impossible to conceal. Expensive, but can one really put a price on staying alive?

Defense Value

Adds a difficulty modifier equal to its value to all attacks made against the wearer. Heavy armor's Defense 10 means attacks take +10.

Damage Reduction (DR)

A flat reduction to basic physical damage, countered by Penetration. Shredding bypasses DR and permanently removes it from the armor until repaired for a resource cost.

Mobility Boost

Normally boosts Run and Sprint by the shown value. Some armor instead penalizes mobility or boosts the Shift movement type.

Adaptive Armor

A pool of bonus HP; all damage comes off it first unless bypassed (e.g. paraphysical attacks). It can't be restored by medical healing, only special items and abilities. Acidized damage is doubled against these armor points.

Barrier

A separate pool of shield or energy points that absorbs incoming damage alongside Adaptive Armor. Electrified damage is doubled against Barrier points.

Upgrade Slots

The number of upgrade modules a piece of armor can hold, letting you tailor it toward your role and loadout.

pages.name: Bleeding Out & Death
pages.html:
SEC-16 // Casualties

Bleeding Out & Death

Absolute //

There is no resurrection in this game. When a character reaches a negative HP value that exceeds their Toughness modifier × 2, they are instantly killed.

Bleeding Out

At 0 HP, or a negative value above the instant-death threshold, a character is bleeding out. At the start of each of their turns they take −2 HP that cannot be reduced. Reaching the death threshold (2 × TGH Mod) means death.

Next of Kin

A replacement character gains no bonus XP or benefits from the previous character's death (though unique base upgrades can raise starting XP). If the body can plausibly be recovered, gear and money pass to a next-of-kin character, possibly with a small cost to repair damaged gear.

pages.name: Status Effects
pages.html:
SEC-17 // Reference

Status Effects

Conditions that affect a character in the field. Browse by category below; each opens a full listing. Many effects carry a (X) value that ticks down by 1 each turn until it disperses at 0.

Negative Effects

Ignited (X)

Take fire damage equal to X at the start of each turn; X drops by 1 each turn until 0.

CURE: Hunker Down, or a 1-action Agility check

All checks take +10 D.M. per X value. Poisoned(3) = +30 to all checks. Ticks down each turn.

CURE: Base Paste

CURE: Warming Gel

Positive Effects

pages.name: Paraphysics: Overview
pages.html:
SEC-18.A // Paraphysics

Paraphysics

How a paraphysical operative is built, advanced, and limited. Tactical casting uses the standard d100 roll under chassis. The Paraphysics skill handles the narrative half.

The Three Currencies

Paraphysical advancement runs on three separate currencies. Each does exactly one job, and none of them substitutes for another.

Currencies
CurrencyControlsUsed To
PsycrystalsAccessUnlock a power at Rank 1. Unlock a power's Rank 5 evolution. Enable paraphysics on a character who did not begin with it (2 crystals).
ExperiencePotency and capacityBuy discipline ranks. Buy power ranks 2, 3 and 4. Buy the Paraphysics skill.
EnergyUse, per missionSpent to cast every power and on improvised paraphysics. Shared with role abilities and melee special strikes.

Psycrystals are loot: found, bought and sold like gear, never a standard currency.

Becoming Paraphysically Enabled

Paraphysics is not open to every operative by default. A character must either be born to it or be forcibly opened to it.

Route One: Creation

A character may begin play paraphysically enabled through their species or their background. Telestoi and Reticulons are born to it, and the Awakened background is open to Humans and Mutants. Khaldar cannot become paraphysically enabled by any means. A paraphysical recruit starts with rank 1 in a discipline and one power at Rank 1, both free. A second rank costs 75 training XP.

Route Two: Awakening

A character who did not begin enabled may be opened to paraphysics in play at a cost of 2 Psycrystals. This is a one time expenditure. Awakening can be taught, but the price stays two crystals whoever does the teaching.

  • The character becomes able to buy and use paraphysics permanently.
  • They gain 1 rank in a discipline of their choice.
  • They may learn one power within that discipline, at Rank 1.

The granted rank opens two power slots. The granted power fills one, and the other waits for a psycrystal. From that point forward they advance on the same tracks as anyone else.

By Species

Casting Attribute and Disciplines
SpeciesCasting AttributeDisciplines Held
HumansCharisma5
TelestoiCharisma3
ReticulonsIntelligence4
KhaldarNone0

Humans cast on Charisma because paraphysics is so new to them that using it is a battle of presence, not knowledge. Telestoi cast on Charisma as a naturally charismatic and emotional people. Reticulons cast on Intelligence: they have lived with it and used it the longest.

pages.name: Paraphysics: Disciplines
pages.html:
SEC-18.B // Paraphysics

Disciplines

A discipline is a school of paraphysical practice and functions as a miniature class in its own right. Ranks are bought with XP alone and cap at Rank 5. Species bonuses may raise an individual cap above 5.

What Discipline Rank Does

The Three Benefits of Discipline Rank
BenefitEffect
AccessGates which powers in that discipline may be unlocked. A power of tier N requires discipline rank N.
CapacityTwo powers per rank held in that discipline. Capacity is per discipline and never pools across schools.
EfficiencyReduces the Energy cost of the powers in that discipline you have outgrown: -1 for each rank above the power's tier.

Discipline rank contributes nothing to accuracy, potency, damage, duration or range. Those live entirely in power ranks.

Costs

Discipline Rank XP Cost
Rank 1Rank 2Rank 3Rank 4Rank 5Total
5075100125150500

Maximum discipline rank at character creation is Rank 2, matching the skill rule, unless the GM states otherwise.

The Disciplines

Open Disciplines
DisciplineTypeOwns
TelekinesisOffense, ControlPush, pull, lift, throw. Forced movement, Pinned, object weaponization.
TelepathyControl, SupportMind Control, Panicked, silent squad comms, memory.
PyrokinesisOffenseIgnited. Area denial and persistent burning terrain.
AstrokinesisOffense, DefenseCover, in both directions. Cosmic damage, mobile soft cover auras, cover bypassing attacks.
VitakinesisSupport, DefenseAll healing. Attribute augmentation, additive Armor HP on allies.
OpticsControl, SupportDisorientated, Concealment, detection, decoys.

Where the Lines Fall

  • The mind: Telepathy acts on cognition and fails entirely against mind immune creatures. Optics acts on perception and does not, so it works on them, and a machine's optical sensor can still be fooled.
  • Movement: Any discipline may grant or deny ordinary movement, never teleportation.
  • Protective cover: Astrokinesis grants mobile soft cover centered on the caster, requiring Concentration, so a flashbang ends it.
  • Squadsight: The squad shares vision, so an Optics reveal is squad wide by default: one action, and every operative can engage that target. Denial is just as severe, removing a target from the whole squad rather than from one shooter.

pages.name: Paraphysics: Powers
pages.html:
SEC-18.C // Paraphysics

Powers and Their Ranks

Every power is its own five rank tree. Entry and apex are gated by psycrystals. Everything between is bought with XP on the player's own schedule.

Power Ranks
RankCostWhat It Does
1 Unlock1 CrystalThe power exists and is usable. Requires discipline rank at least equal to the power's tier, and an open slot in that discipline. Nothing stops a caster filling a new slot with a lower tier power.
2 Advancement20 XPThe first step on the power's tracks: Accuracy -10, Potency +4.
3 Choice40 XPSelect one modification from those the power offers. The power's only choice node, and it is permanent.
4 Advancement60 XPThe second and larger step: Accuracy a further -15 (-25 total), Potency a further +6 (+10 total).
5 Evolution1 CrystalThe power reaches its final form, written for that power alone. Where a power offers more than one evolution you pick one, and the choice is permanent.

A full power costs 120 XP and 2 crystals. Each power writes out its own ranks, so its card is the final word on what it gains at each one.

Profile Tracks

Each power advances along two of five tracks, chosen to suit what the power is for. No power advances all five.

The Five Tracks
TrackWhat It Moves
AccuracyAttack D.M. on the d100 casting roll. -10 at Rank 2, -25 total at Rank 4.
PotencyD.M. imposed on the target's saving throw. +4 at Rank 2, +10 total at Rank 4.
DamageDice or flat bonus on damaging powers.
DurationRounds an effect persists, where applicable.
RangeOptimal range band in tiles.

Modifications

Rank 3 draws on a shared library. Each power offers two or three, and its own numbers may differ from the summary here.

Modification Archetypes
ModificationEffect
LingeringEffect duration extended.
ChainJumps to a second target at reduced effect.
PiercingIgnores a defense it normally respects.
OverloadSpend additional Energy for scaled effect.
ReflexiveUsable as a reaction.
WideSingle target becomes a small area.
EfficientEnergy cost 1 less, never below half its base.
AnchoredNo longer requires Concentration. On some powers it instead means the Concentration can only be dropped by the caster at will.
AdaptiveYou may for the added cost of +1 Energy change the attribute required to save from this power.

Where a modification or evolution costs extra Energy, you choose at each cast whether to pay it. Unpaid, the power goes off as its standard version. Some powers offer modes chosen at cast, and some powers are mutually exclusive: taking one closes the other for good.

pages.name: Paraphysics: Casting
pages.html:
SEC-18.D // Paraphysics

Resolution in Combat

Tactical casting uses the standard d100 roll under chassis. Nothing here is a separate subsystem.

Attack Powers

Roll 1d100 and apply modifiers. The result must land at or under the caster's casting attribute.

Modifiers on a Paraphysical Attack
SourceValue
Power rank (Accuracy track)-10 at Rank 2, -25 at Rank 4
In Optimal Range2x casting modifier
Out of Optimal Range+15. Optimal range is set per power.
Paraphysical focus-20, sharing the -25 ceiling with the Accuracy track
Cover+30 half, +45 full
Target armor DefenseAs armor
Example // Gravbolt

Ragnar casts Gravbolt (Rank 4, Accuracy track at -25) against a GENESIS trooper in half cover, In Optimal Range. His Charisma is 55, so his modifier is 5.

1d100 - 25 (Power Rank) - 10 (2x CHA, IOR) + 6 (Trooper Armor) + 30 (Half Cover)
Rolls 46 // 46 - 35 + 36 = 47

47 is at or under 55. Gravbolt hits. A focus would add nothing here: at Rank 4 the Accuracy track already fills the -25 ceiling.

The Paraphysical Focus

A focus gives -20 on attack powers, but the focus and the Accuracy track together never exceed -25. It carries a fledgling power and is redundant for a power at Rank 4. Because the ceiling is per power, a caster with several low rank powers keeps wanting one.

The focus counts against carry capacity, cannot be concealed, and is not expected to take mods. A low rank caster on an infiltration mission chooses between the focus and getting through the checkpoint.

Saving Throw Powers

The target rolls 1d100 and must land at or under the attribute the power tests. The caster adds to that roll:

Save D.M. = casting modifier + Potency track (+4 at Rank 2, +10 at Rank 4)

Damage and Defenses

  • Most paraphysical attacks bypass the Ablative Armor pool. Damage goes to barriers first, then to HP.
  • Most paraphysics deal non standard damage types (Cold, Electric, Psychic and so on). The target consults their DR table. Psychic and Cosmic DR start at 0.
  • Paraphysics are unaffected by Suppressing Fire.

Concentration

A caster can hold Concentration on one power at a time, and concentrating on a new power lets the old one go. The Disorientated condition breaks it, making a flashbang a cheap and universally available counter. Every power that requires Concentration says so on its card. An area centered on the caster is drawn around their token and lasts as long as the power does.

Barriers

A paraphysical barrier shares one pool with armor barriers, needs no armor to hold, and never stacks: it lifts your Barrier to its value rather than adding on top.

pages.name: Paraphysics: Energy
pages.html:
SEC-18.E // Paraphysics

Energy

Paraphysics draws on the same Energy pool as role abilities, melee special strikes and chemthrower bursts. Your pool is your species' Base Energy plus your Charisma bonus plus your Intelligence bonus, and perks can raise it substantially.

The Discipline Discount

  • -1 Energy for each discipline rank above the power's tier. A power costs its listed price at the rank that unlocks it and gets cheaper only as you outgrow it. A tier 5 power is never discounted.
  • Applies only to powers with a base cost of 4 or more.
  • Hard floor: half base cost, rounded up, across all sources combined. This covers the Efficient modification as well, so a 5 cost power never drops below 3 regardless of how many reductions stack.

Energy Cost by Tier

Base Costs
Power TierBase Cost
12 to 3
23 to 4
34 to 5
46 to 7
58 to 10
  • Area or multiple targets: the top of the tier's band.
  • Concentration: the bottom of the band, since a flashbang can end it.
  • Squad wide Optics effects: +1.

Energy does not regenerate in the field without specific items, so a failed cast still costs you.

pages.name: Paraphysics: Skill and Improvisation
pages.html:
SEC-18.F // Paraphysics

The Paraphysics Skill

The Paraphysics skill is a normal DYNOSRS skill bought with XP. It governs the narrative half of paraphysics and never touches tactical casting accuracy or potency.

What the Skill Covers
UseRequires Discipline Ranks?
Identifying paraphysical anomalies in the fieldNo
Knowledge of paraphysics, practitioners and phenomenaNo
Improvising effects outside combat where no explicit power covers the attemptYes

The first two uses are open to anyone who trains the skill, including characters who are not paraphysically enabled.

Improvised Paraphysics

A character with ranks in a discipline may attempt effects within that discipline that no power of theirs covers.

  • Out of combat only, meaning outside initiative. There is no in combat exception.
  • The effect must sit within a discipline the character holds ranks in. No improvising outside your schools.
  • Difficulty scales with reach. An effect within the character's discipline rank is a standard check. One tier beyond is Hard. Two tiers beyond is Formidable. Three or more is outside what the character can attempt.
  • It costs Energy, set by the GM against the same bands as powers, sized to the effect attempted.
  • If a power covers it, you need the power. Improvisation produces effects that powers do not. It does not produce cheaper versions of effects that powers do.
Reading a Paraphysics Improvisation Roll
ResultOutcome
Success, cleanThe effect occurs as described.
Success with DangerThe effect occurs with a complication: additional Energy drawn, attention attracted, an unintended secondary consequence, or a lingering disturbance at the site.
FailureThe effect does not occur. Energy is still spent.
DefeatParaphysical mishap. The GM may invert the intended effect, inflict a condition on the caster, or let the attempt reach something that should have stayed unreached.

pages.name: Strategy: Overview
pages.html:
SEC-19.A // Strategy Layer

The Strategy Layer

The rebellion against the invaders is a world war unlike any other. Countless resistance groups across the globe fight small battles with GENESIS, but without support and greater coordination these efforts will prove futile. The ODR can fill this need, and in turn these resistance groups are willing to pledge their support in the fight against GENESIS.

It is this combined effort that gives the fight to retake Earth any chance of success. The ODR, for all their knowledge and superior equipment, are far too few in number to hold any liberated territory. The Long War can only be won when soldiers and civilians alike are willing to throw off their chains and take a stand for what they believe in.

What is the Strategy Layer?

The strategy layer is meant to capture the feeling of being in a war room, looking over maps and formulating the overarching plans that turn the effort to liberate Earth from a vague ambition into a defined and actionable strategy.

This creates narratives and a greater intent behind tactical actions than simply killing all the enemies on the map. Consider two squads:

  • Squad A is trying to keep a low profile while collecting information on a major GENESIS asset to sabotage.
  • Squad B is gathering supplies and materials in a smash-and-grab raid before reinforcements show up.

The targets chosen, the equipment loadout taken, and the tactical approaches used will vary significantly between them.

These tactical actions then filter up into the strategy layer. They provide useful information and material while drawing GENESIS attention away from important infrastructure, which can then be destroyed to soften up Megacities for assault.

The Long War cannot be won solely through force of arms. A keen mind that can understand the enemy, their weaknesses, and how to best exploit them can accomplish far more than brute force ever could.

Retaking Earth

The struggle to retake Earth is a truly massive endeavor. To decisively defeat GENESIS, all Megacities in an area must be successfully taken over. For the purposes of our playtest, Neo Seattle will be the goal.

Megacity Objectives

Every Megacity has three assets that must be taken:

  1. A military citadel
  2. A motor pool
  3. A center of government

Once all three are captured, GENESIS' ability to contest the Resistance is effectively shattered in that area. The Megacity and surrounding regions are considered liberated.

Liberated Region Bonuses

  • Each Megacity has a unique landmark that can provide bonuses.
  • Liberated Megacities count as ODR bases for any Strategy Layer action.
  • Negative events in a liberated region are automatically handled by Resistance forces and don't require ODR attention, unless stated otherwise.
  • GENESIS ground forces cannot move through a liberated region unless a Reprisal mission is successful there first.

Campaign Scope

For the moment, only the West Coast of the United States is fully mapped out, and we consider the typical campaign to be similar in scope. However, because these systems are designed to be scalable, you could run an entire campaign in a smaller area like a single Megacity, or scale it up to require liberating the entire world.

Numbers in These Pages

Every number the turn engine uses is a default the GM can change in Configure Settings, under Strategy Layer. These pages show the defaults.

pages.name: Strategy: GENESIS Regions
pages.html:
SEC-19.B // Strategy Layer

GENESIS Regions

GENESIS has nominal control over Earth. This control is broken down into regions, each with two statistics: Strength and Heat.

Strength

Strength represents the concentration of power in a region, from 0 to 25. Higher values allow for denser deployments of higher quality units.

  • Low Strength: patrols of a few troopers.
  • High Strength: elite Xar'Nath squads with paraphysical specialists and close air support.

Regions that GENESIS projects power from will have high Strength, so direct attacks against them are often suicidal. However, the ODR can exploit the sluggish and reactive nature of GENESIS. By undertaking operations in other regions to either bolster the resistance or subvert the aliens, GENESIS is forced to react. Strength will be redirected to these other regions, allowing convoys of soldiers to be ambushed and leaving the vaunted cities and fortresses of GENESIS open to attack.

Heat

Heat is a measure of how alert the GENESIS forces in a region are. There are five Heat levels:

Heat Levels
LevelExample Response
NonePolice response before military units are mobilized.
LowMilitary units are mobilized first, in ground transports.
MediumAlien and GENESIS units arrive by air and ground at greater speed. Stratagems and combat vehicles start to be deployed.
HighElite soldiers drop on the squad's position from orbit within minutes.
MaximumAlien combat units are teleported to the squad's position.

Heat is the primary statistic GENESIS considers when moving forces on the strategy layer, and it controls how quickly and aggressively they respond to resistance activity.

Note

It might be tempting to ignore locations with high Strength or Heat and focus solely on low-risk areas. However, some research and upgrades can only be unlocked by fighting enemies and salvaging equipment that only consistently deploy at higher Heat or Strength levels.

Raising and Lowering Heat

GENESIS is a highly reactive force.

  • Heat increases as GENESIS soldiers and assets are attacked. More important assets, like military bases or propaganda centers, increase Heat by far more than a few skirmishes. This can be a great way to draw attention away from your real target while getting some good equipment in the process.
  • Heat decreases by 1 level in regions where no tactical actions or relevant events have taken place for two turns.
  • Increases or decreases in Heat take effect at the beginning of the next strategy layer turn.
Heat Raised by an Action
ActionHeatExample
Minor+1A skirmish or ambush
Major+2A security station or VIP
Critical+3A base or propaganda center

pages.name: Strategy: The Resistance
pages.html:
SEC-19.C // Strategy Layer

The Resistance

The struggle against GENESIS is an uphill battle, but properly supplied and supported, the Resistance can prove to be stalwart and capable fighters. The Resistance's ability to combat the invaders is measured by Logistics and Reputation.

  • Logistics covers all forms of supply and material concerns, from food stores to ammunition and medicine.
  • Reputation governs the popularity of the Resistance among the general population, as well as their willingness to rise up and fight their alien overlords.

Keeping the Resistance supplied and liked by the people is essential for long-term success, as the ODR cannot hold the vast swathes of liberated territory by themselves.

Logistics

Logistics is the currency of the strategy layer and encompasses all forms of goods that can be used directly or traded for something that can be.

Gaining Logistics

  • Performing missions in a region
  • Certain event cards

Spending Logistics

  • Support in tactical battles (see below)
  • Researching new equipment
  • Building regional upgrades

Losing Logistics

  • Certain event cards
  • Successful GENESIS Reprisals

Logistics are meant to be used, not hoarded, as equipment is far more expendable than a skilled soldier.

General Uses of Logistics
SupportCostEffect
Reinforcements10Resistance soldiers break cover and assist you. They deploy nearby and follow the squad's orders. While they may not be the most skilled, sometimes a few extra guns are all it takes to change the outcome of a battle.
Inside Job10 to 25The Resistance uses one of their many connections to your benefit, from something as simple as an unlocked door to delaying GENESIS' response time. GM discretion, but this cannot directly interact with GENESIS forces. Cost depends on what is asked for.
Hidden Cache15Request the location of hidden Resistance supplies. A nearby location will contain items useful for the situation at hand. The GM should be as helpful as possible when choosing items without directly solving the problem.
Mortar Strike30Designate three non-overlapping areas on the map. Roll three d100s; any roll of 75+ causes that strike to scatter 1d4 tiles. Each mortar deals 3d4+4 damage, radius 3, Destructive 6.
Emergency Extraction50Call for an emergency evacuation to escape a potentially lethal situation. It generally takes at least 1 full combat round to arrive. Initially an armored civilian transport is available, but more options can be discovered over time.

Reputation

It's been true across time that no insurgency can succeed without the support of the people, and here it is no different. The Resistance's Reputation in a region approximates how popular and supported the Resistance is by the general populace.

Reputation runs on nine levels: Hostile, Resentful, Wary, Uneasy, Neutral, Sympathetic, Friendly, Supportive, Devoted. Each level holds a 10 point bar. When the bar fills the level rises, and when it empties the level falls. Either way the new level starts at 5 and any overflow is thrown away, so Reputation is hard to move and easy to hold.

Reputation Points
CausePoints
Successful mission+2
Partly successful mission+1
Failed mission-2
An undeniable failure, or civilians negatively affected by the ODR's actions-4
Each step of Reputation on a card, including GENESIS Propaganda3

Effects of Reputation

  • High Reputation (Friendly and above): Civilians might look the other way, or even stick their necks out for the ODR of their own will, potentially buying just enough time for the squad to escape.
  • Low Reputation (Wary and below): People might call GENESIS if the squad is spotted, or even attack them to curry favor with the aliens.

Reputation can often be the intangible edge the squad needs to get away, as even the smallest help at the right time can be the difference between life and death.

Factions

Standing with each major and minor faction runs on the same nine level bar as Reputation, from At War, Hostile, Unfriendly, Wary, Neutral, Cordial, Friendly, Trusted, Allied. Factions offer tasks each turn, and players send their own operatives to work them. A task done earns +2 standing with its faction, and a task failed costs -2.

Intel

Intel is an uncommon secondary resource the Resistance uses to locate GENESIS assets or specific resources like exotic Research Salvage.

  • Obtained only through: breaching GENESIS security, interrogating VIPs, or other forms of espionage.
  • Used to: boost Intelligence Actions and execute more exotic and powerful stratagems.

pages.name: Strategy: Turns
pages.html:
SEC-19.D // Strategy Layer

Strategy Turns

Each strategy layer turn represents one week of in-universe time and runs through three phases: GENESIS Phase, Event Phase, ODR Phase, then repeat.

GENESIS Phase

Order of operations:

  1. Every 8 turns: Each Megacity region gains +1 Strength.
  2. Strength moves: GENESIS moves Strength to adjacent regions with a higher Heat value, preferring to transfer Strength from rural and wildland regions first, then slums, then Megacities. A region pulls 3 Strength from one cooler neighbor each turn.
  3. Heat adjusts: Heat values increase or decrease based on regional activity.
  4. Every 4 turns: The GM draws 3 Dark Event cards and picks 2 to use. Dark Event cards must be used in the same turn they are drawn unless the card indicates otherwise.
  5. Discretionary cards: The GM may play any discretionary Dark Event cards. Only one Reprisal card can be used at a time if multiple are available.

A liberated region sits out the GENESIS Phase.

Event Phase

The Event Phase occurs every 2nd turn. Order of operations:

  1. Clear old events: If persistent event cards are in play, discard them and apply their discard effects, if any.
  2. Draw: The GM draws 3 Event cards face down, and 1 World Event.
  3. Distribute: Place the cards at random across the regions, no more than one card per region.
  4. Reveal all cards.
  5. Apply effects. Instantaneous cards apply immediately and are then discarded. Persistent cards (effects that can be interacted with or countered) stay on the region until the end of the next strategy layer turn, then are discarded.
Note

Some cards have effects that only activate when discarded, or amplify their effects when discarded.

ODR Phase

The ODR Phase is the player phase and the most involved. Actions are taken in this order:

  1. Research Actions
  2. Engineering Actions
  3. Intelligence Actions
  4. Tactical Actions

Once all actions are taken, the current strategy layer turn ends and the cycle begins anew.

pages.name: Strategy: Research Actions
pages.html:
SEC-19.E // Strategy Layer

Research Actions

Research covers all forms of investigation into materials, both mundane and alien, and how they can be applied to bolster the ODR's effort to retake the planet.

Research typically doesn't provide benefits on its own. Instead, it unlocks equipment or unique services that ODR operatives can purchase at will, like better weaponry or genetic modifications. While it might not provide immediate benefits, research is essential to the war effort, as it will even the playing field and allow the ODR to step out of the shadows and contest the aliens directly.

Rules

  • Only one research project can be undertaken at a time.
  • You can switch to a different project at any point with no penalty.

Progressing Research

  • Passive progress: 10 Logistics per strategy layer turn.
  • Spending Logistics: The intended way to complete research quickly.
  • Assigned soldiers: Each soldier contributes additional Logistics per turn equal to their Intelligence bonus + 5 per rank in the relevant skill. The soldier must have one of the project's Specialization skills. A soldier can only contribute using one skill, even if they have several qualifying skills, and can only be assigned to one project at a time.
  • Specialized Salvage: Scientists worked fervently during the war to close the technology gap, and GENESIS has plenty of useful resources that can be stolen by an enterprising rebel. Salvage locations can be pinpointed using Long Term Intelligence Actions. Each recovered salvage contributes progress equal to 30% of the project's Logistics cost.

Research Project Format

Project Fields
FieldMeaning
NameThe title of the project.
SpecializationThe skills associated with the project. Soldiers with at least one of these skills contribute extra Logistics per turn.
AdvancementThe category of research the project belongs to. Pursuing this project unlocks more projects of those types.
CostThe Logistics required to complete the project. Varies from project to project.
UnlocksThe types of equipment unlocked. Exact details are only provided after the project is complete.
DescriptionAn in-setting overview of what the project entails.
Example // Armory Refit

Specialization: Mechanics, Technology. Advancement: Weaponry, Armor. Cost: X Logistics. Unlocks: Weapon and Armor Modifications.

With the base up and running we've begun taking stock of our equipment's capabilities. While a majority of it survived intact some important tools did not. Sourcing sufficient replacements won't be too difficult and allow us to create some basic modifications and get the most out of what we have before we can create something new.

pages.name: Strategy: Engineering Actions
pages.html:
SEC-19.F // Strategy Layer

Engineering Actions

Engineering Actions cover all forms of infrastructure building, as well as the maintenance and deployment of larger assets like vehicles.

Engineering projects typically provide immediate benefits to the region where they were built, affect the ODR as a whole, or provide unique tactical assets that change how squads approach situations.

Rules

  • Up to 3 Engineering Actions can be active at a time, and all active projects progress passively, 10 Logistics per turn.
  • Projects are completed using Logistics.
  • Upgrades built via Engineering Actions can be destroyed in GENESIS Reprisal actions.

Assigning Soldiers

Contributions
Contribution TypeRequirementBonus per Turn
SpecialistA skill matching the project's SpecializationIntelligence bonus + 5 per rank in the relevant skill
LaborAny soldier (unless stated otherwise)Strength bonus

Engineering Action Examples

Regional Upgrade // SAM Site

Affects only the region it is built in. Specialization: Mechanics, Technology. Cost: X Logistics.

A Surface-to-Air Missile Site can interdict aircraft and force them to move in less than ideal ways to respond to problems safely. Increases the time it takes for GENESIS to respond via air and decreases the strength of Reprisals in this area.

Base Upgrade // Training Facility

Augments the ODR as a faction. Specialization: Tactics, History. Cost: X Logistics.

Any ODR operative under 200 XP is immediately brought up to 200 XP. All new characters start at 200 XP.

pages.name: Strategy: Intelligence Actions
pages.html:
SEC-19.G // Strategy Layer

Intelligence Actions

Intelligence Actions cover locating areas rich in resources, or GENESIS assets that need to be destroyed to undermine the aliens' control and draw Strength away from Megacities.

There are two categories:

  • Short Term: Locate specific resources the ODR needs to achieve victory, often in greater quantities than what can be found on most missions.
  • Long Term: Locate major assets, counter Dark Events, or stop a regional crisis.

You may run one Short Term and one Long Term action at the same time.

Progressing Intelligence Actions

  • Passive progress: 10 Intel per strategy layer turn, on each active action. This is progress, not Intel added to your stock.
  • Assigned soldiers: Soldiers with any Social skill, Stealth, Hacking, or Lockpicking each contribute Intel per turn equal to the skill's attribute modifier + 5 per rank in the skill. A perk that counts another skill on Intelligence Actions lets that skill contribute too.
  • Spending Intel: Intel can be spent to progress Intelligence Actions. If things are balanced as intended, it should ideally be spent on Long Term actions to complete them in a reasonable timeframe.
Examples
Short TermLong Term
Locate Research SalvageLocate GENESIS Assets
Find Alloy SalvageCounter Dark Events
Locate Aetherite StockpileIdentify Source of Regional Crisis
Collect IntelLocate Major Collaborator
Locate Valuable ItemsIdentify Vulnerable Supply Depot
Find Logistics CacheCultivate Faction Favor

Intelligence Actions are required to affect Strength and Heat more dramatically without attacking installations outright.

pages.name: Strategy: Tactical Actions
pages.html:
SEC-19.H // Strategy Layer

Tactical Actions

Tactical Actions are the ODR deciding what to actually take action against that turn.

  • One Tactical Action can be taken per strategy layer turn.
  • Tactical Actions are taken at the end of the turn, and completing one advances the strategy layer to the next round.
  • Once a Tactical Action is chosen, a mission is generated for soldiers to deploy on.
  • Some Tactical Actions are always available; others must be revealed by Intelligence Actions.

Always-available Tactical Actions typically reward fewer resources, but provide a consistent flow of material and experience and are the easiest for new characters.

Always Available
ActionRewards and Notes
Ambush PatrolsCorpses, valuables, loot. Minor Logistics, minor Heat.
Scavenge for Basic ResourcesLogistics, alloys, valuables, etc.
Low-Priority GENESIS Security StationsHigher risk than the above, but greater rewards.
Obvious GENESIS Assets
Respond to Distress CallsIf available.
Respond to Events or Dark EventsIf available.
Low-Priority VIP Extraction or AssassinationHigh Heat manipulation, plus Intel if captured.

Losing Ground

When a region is liberated, nearby Megacities and their surrounding regions spike in Heat, and Strength begins to concentrate there. Once an adjacent region reaches a certain amount of Strength, GENESIS launches an Incursion to retake the liberated region. This prompts a high-priority mission to kneecap the Incursion so the Resistance can handle the rest.

  • The spike: Regions within 2 borders of the liberated area gain +2 Heat, up to Maximum.
  • The Incursion: It launches when a neighbor of a liberated region reaches 20 Strength.
  • Stopping it: The ODR has 1 turn. A broken Incursion costs the staging region 8 Strength.
  • If it lands: The target becomes Contested, and 8 Strength moves in from the staging region.
